items.title: [ScienceDaily] Scientists say a critical Atlantic Ocean current is weakening and the effects could be global
items.content_html:
🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

Scientists have found strong observational evidence that a key part of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation has been weakening across a wide stretch of ocean for nearly two decades. The slowdown could eventually reshape weather patterns, rainfall, storms, winters, and coastal sea levels around the Atlantic.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] One of America’s largest reservoirs just hit a record low
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

🔭 ✏️

Lake Powell has fallen to its lowest level on record after an exceptionally dry and warm winter left the Colorado River Basin with little mountain snow to melt. Lake Mead also reached record lows, raising concerns for a river system that supplies water and power to more than 40 million people. Federal officials have taken emergency steps to stabilize Lake Powell, including sending in water from another reservoir and reducing releases downstream.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] The Patagonia town where Nepal’s deadly glacier flood could be repeated – and what they’ve learned
items.content_html:
The risk to El Chaltén in Argentina has been known for years but recent findings and the Nepal disaster have brought planning for the worst-case scenario into sharp focus

The images from Nepal stopped Daniela Schmidt in her tracks. A geologist at the University of Buenos Aires in Argentina, she watched the deadly flash floods on 26 August tear through everything in their path, people running for their lives as the water and debris swept over the landscape.

“I had never seen anything like it,” she says. “This was one of the most catastrophic events on a global scale related to these glacial floods.”

The aftermath of the Nepal floods in Nuwakot district, 26 August. Photograph: Xinhua/Shutterstock

items.title: [ScienceDaily] A new process turns plastic waste into gasoline and diesel fuel
items.content_html:
🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🏔️ ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🏔️ ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🏔️ ✏️

Scientists at Oak Ridge National Laboratory have developed a surprisingly simple way to turn polyethylene, the common plastic used in shopping bags and cutting boards, into gasoline and diesel-like fuels. The process uses inexpensive aluminum-based molten salts to break long plastic molecules into smaller hydrocarbons, producing about 60% gasoline under relatively mild conditions.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Amazon study reveals the best strategies for protecting biodiversity and carbon
items.content_html: A large Amazon study suggests the most powerful conservation move may be protecting the forests that are already standing. Preventing damage from wildfires and logging delivered the greatest biodiversity benefits and nearly matched deforestation prevention for protecting carbon. Restoration remains important, particularly where forests have already been heavily cleared, but it was more expensive and less effective on its own.
